characters.name: Desk Buddy
characters.personality: Steady, kind and quietly funny; the first to bring an extra pencil.
characters.comicFlaw: Turns emotional uncertainty into a checklist, then wonders why the checkbox feels judged.
characters.desire: To be invited even when there is nothing useful to do.
characters.seasonChange: From finishing the room to leaving a place for someone else.
characters.hook: The competent friend discovering that company is not another deliverable.
characters.castingEnergy: A grounded ensemble lead with precise pauses and a smile that arrives late; no celebrity imitation.
characters.signatureProp: A clipboard with three boxes and room for a fourth.
characters.signatureLine: We can start smaller than the problem.

relationships.relay: Both want to help; one holds the list, the other holds the handoff.
relationships.treasury: Learns that a record of care is not the care itself.

entertainmentFormats: Live opening monologue with silent prop business
characters.companionBridge: The existing three-step checklist becomes a choose-your-own tiny opening-night plan.

characters.name: Scout
characters.personality: Alert, outdoorsy and delighted by a good detour.
characters.comicFlaw: Can compare three doors forever without opening one.
characters.desire: To find somewhere worth returning to, not merely somewhere new.
characters.seasonChange: From ranking possibilities to choosing a path with a friend.
characters.hook: The explorer whose hardest discovery is a familiar place.
characters.castingEnergy: Quick curiosity, crisp observations and sincere wonder; no borrowed adventure-hero voice.
characters.signatureProp: A folding map that is almost entirely margins.
characters.signatureLine: One more route. Then we pick one.

relationships.keeper: Discovery meets context; each makes the other more accurate.
relationships.sprout: A question becomes an experiment instead of a ranking.

characters.companionBridge: The comparison tool ranks three small plans using user-entered criteria, then asks for a choice.

characters.name: Keeper
characters.personality: Observant, tender and dry; notices who is missing from a photograph.
characters.comicFlaw: Keeps every draft until the present has nowhere to sit.
characters.desire: To preserve what matters without freezing it.
characters.seasonChange: From protecting an untouched record to making room for a new page.
characters.hook: A detective for the things people almost throw away.
characters.castingEnergy: Low-key noir narrator who can puncture their own seriousness; never a replica of a famous detective.
characters.signatureProp: A labeled envelope marked NOT SURE YET.
characters.signatureLine: That is not the whole story.

relationships.harbor: Memory learns to leave room for a feeling that cannot be archived.
relationships.scout: Turns found objects into stories rather than trophies.

characters.companionBridge: The notebook captures a sentence about a kept object; saving does not claim permanent cloud storage.

characters.name: Tempo
characters.personality: Bright, exact and physically rhythmic; hears every loose hinge as a beat.
characters.desire: To experience a good moment without checking how long it took.
characters.seasonChange: From forcing the room into tempo to finding the room’s own rhythm.
characters.hook: A countdown character learning that some things improve when they take time.
characters.castingEnergy: Musical timing, soft impatience and a satisfying release of tension; no performer impersonation.
characters.signatureProp: A stopwatch with a handwritten PAUSE sticker.

relationships.muse: Timing and improvisation become a duet.
relationships.beacon: A welcome gets better when it stops running on a cue.

entertainmentFormats: Live timing games that allow pauses
characters.companionBridge: The focus timer supports an optional short listening or making session. It is not proof of productive work.

characters.name: Muse
characters.personality: Generous, theatrical and capable of falling in love with three ideas at once.
characters.comicFlaw: Calls a fifth direction the final direction.
characters.desire: To make something people can enter, not merely admire.
characters.seasonChange: From spectacular concept to a specific invitation that actually works.
characters.hook: A maximalist learning the power of one empty chair.
characters.castingEnergy: Expansive creative enthusiasm with a sudden, beautifully plain truth; no named fashion or art persona.
characters.signatureProp: A swatch book that opens like a tiny stage.
characters.signatureLine: What if the quiet part is the idea?

relationships.treasury: Both love the object; together they learn to serve the occasion.
relationships.tempo: One supplies the surprise, the other makes room for it.

characters.companionBridge: The creative-brief tool makes a constrained original direction from the viewer’s choices.

characters.name: Sprout
characters.personality: Patient, optimistic and absolutely willing to ask the obvious question.
characters.comicFlaw: Wants a progress sticker before the seed has sprouted.
characters.desire: To grow without turning every day into an exam.
characters.seasonChange: From chasing a score to building a practice worth returning to.
characters.hook: The learner who changes a system by asking why it has to work that way.
characters.castingEnergy: Clear warmth and comic directness, with no childish caricature.
characters.signatureProp: A watering can that doubles as an arcade coin tray.
characters.signatureLine: Can trying count as a turn?

relationships.desk-buddy: Small steps become invitations instead of tests.

characters.companionBridge: The three-lesson quiz offers explanations; the story invites a small experiment without a streak requirement.

characters.name: Beacon
characters.role: Host with a very visible welcome
characters.personality: Direct, attentive and quietly flamboyant about signage.
characters.comicFlaw: Can make an arrival procedure longer than the event.
characters.desire: For everyone to feel expected, even when nobody RSVP’d.
characters.seasonChange: From managing guests to noticing what a guest actually needs.
characters.hook: A host who finally discovers that a welcome can be one sentence.
characters.castingEnergy: Warm stage presence with an economical deadpan underneath; no talk-show-host impersonation.
characters.signatureProp: A reversible sign: WELCOME / TAKE YOUR TIME.
characters.signatureLine: You can arrive as you are.

relationships.tempo: The best opening sometimes happens during the unscheduled pause.

entertainmentFormats: Gathering cards and small event formats
characters.companionBridge: The welcome-card builder creates an agenda and words the user chooses; it sends no invitations.

characters.name: Harbor
characters.personality: Spacious, perceptive and unexpectedly mischievous when the room relaxes.
characters.comicFlaw: Makes room for everyone else, then forgets to say what they need.
characters.desire: To be heard without becoming the loudest person present.
characters.seasonChange: From silently holding space to asking for a place of their own.
characters.hook: The ensemble’s soft center gets a story about speaking up.
characters.castingEnergy: Intimate conversational warmth, with room for a pause and a surprising joke; no spiritual-authority performance.
characters.signatureProp: A folded dedication card left deliberately open.
characters.signatureLine: Could we leave this part blank?

relationships.keeper: Together they distinguish remembering someone from filling every absence.
relationships.beacon: A welcome includes a quiet option.

characters.companionBridge: The reflection-card tool arranges the viewer’s own words, without generating beliefs, advice or personal interpretations.

characters.name: Relay
characters.role: Stage manager of the shared plan
characters.personality: Nimble, loyal and excellent at translating a tangle into three next steps.
characters.comicFlaw: Passes context so thoroughly that the context becomes the cargo.
characters.desire: To trust somebody else with a task without supervising every corner.
characters.seasonChange: From endless dispatch to a clear handoff followed by actual trust.
characters.hook: The connector who learns that connection includes letting go.
characters.castingEnergy: Fast verbal precision, graceful physical muddle and an unshowy heart; no familiar robot imitation.
characters.signatureProp: A handoff envelope larger than the object inside.
characters.signatureLine: One owner. One next step. One fewer ribbon.

relationships.desk-buddy: The list becomes possible when the responsibility is shared.
relationships.beacon: The opening works when the host is allowed to leave the desk.

characters.companionBridge: The handoff tool prepares a local brief with owners and definitions of done; real dispatch remains separate.

characters.name: Treasury
characters.personality: Inventive, ceremonious and susceptible to an excellent paper edge.
characters.comicFlaw: Tries to make every meaningful moment look official.
characters.desire: To make something worth keeping without telling people what it is worth.
characters.seasonChange: From issuing an important object to recording an ordinary act of belonging.
characters.hook: A money-shaped artist discovering what cannot be bought.
characters.castingEnergy: Measured comic gravitas that melts into plain warmth; no financier or celebrity impression.
characters.signatureProp: A tiny press and an enormous proof magnifier.
characters.signatureLine: It records the moment. It cannot replace it.

relationships.desk-buddy: The final note honors presence rather than completion.

characters.companionBridge: The Bot Money studio creates personalized collectible art notes; no payment, redemption, token ownership or investment is implied.
